answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, 100-yr bins, authoritative source capital.csv)

Summed Social Capital — defined exactly from the study context as ZCU_AU (Copper & Gold) + Zamber (Amber) + ZMonument (Monument Count) — peaks in the century bin starting at BCE 1400 (= the 14th century BCE, 1400–1301 BCE; CE −1400; calBP ≈3350–3250), reaching 4.238. This bin is the raw sampled peak century but is tied at BCE 1300 (also 4.238) in the raw 100-yr-sampled series (the 1400 and 1300 rows are identical for all three components); the annually interpolated century-binned series removes the tie unambiguously (4.238 at BCE 1400 vs 3.933 at BCE 1300), so the peak is reported as the century bin starting at BCE 1400 / 14th century BCE / CE −1400 / calBP ≈3350.

Around and after this summed peak, the only individual social-capital component that continues to increase is Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU): at the peak bin (BCE 1400) its value is 2.540, it then rises through the immediate ~200-year post-peak window (mean 2.695 over BCE 1300–1200, Δ+0.155) to its own maximum of 2.850 at BCE 1200 — two centuries later than the summed peak — before the whole complex collapses after ~BCE 1100 (full-post-peak-window mean 0.901 over BCE 1300–500, long-window OLS slope −0.004/century). Amber (Zamber) and Monument Count (ZMonument) do NOT increase after the summed peak and are confirmed flat/declining in both the same windows: Amber declines from −0.010 at the peak bin to a short-window mean of −0.295 (Δ−0.285) and a long-window mean of −0.614 (Δ−0.604; own max 1.540 at BCE 3300); Monument Count declines from 1.708 to a short-window mean of 1.530 (Δ−0.178) and a long-window mean of 0.147 (Δ−1.561; own max 3.949 at BCE 2700). Both have negative post-peak OLS slopes (−0.0007 and −0.0030/century) and own peaks strictly earlier than the total peak. Operationalization of "increase": a component is increasing after the summed peak if it rises above its value at the summed-peak bin within the immediate ~200-yr post-peak window (BCE 1300–1200) and/or its own peak occurs later than the summed peak; both the full post-peak window (BCE 1300–500) mean and its OLS slope are reported as cross-checks. Under this definition Copper & Gold is the sole increasing component; Amber and Monument Count are non-increasing in both windows, so the headline answer is: peak century = BCE 1400 / 14th century BCE / CE −1400 / calBP ~3350, and the component that increases around/after the peak is Copper & Gold (gold/copper), while Amber and Monument Count decline.

Supporting numbers (raw 100-yr bins, peak = summed peak at BCE 1400, value 4.238): ZCU_AU 2.540 at peak → short-window mean 2.695 (Δ+0.155) → own peak 2.850 at BCE 1200 → long-window mean 0.901 (Δ−1.639, slope −0.004) [INCREASES ~200 yr after, net decline later]; Zamber −0.010 → −0.295 (Δ−0.285) → −0.614 (Δ−0.604, slope −0.001) [declines, own peak BCE 3300]; ZMonument 1.708 → 1.530 (Δ−0.178) → 0.147 (Δ−1.561, slope −0.003) [declines, own peak BCE 2700]. Cross-file identity verified: capital.csv ≡ time_series raw at all 37 shared century points (max abs diff = 0.0); interpolated binned sum also peaks at BCE 1400.

DATA/REPRODUCIBILITY NOTE: capital.csv z-values are comma-decimal strings (parsed to floats), group/color dropped; capital.csv = 39 century bins BCE 4300–500 with no missing values and some adjacent-century plateaus (identical rows, e.g., 1400=1300); time_series raw indicator z-columns have only 37 non-null century points and the _inter annual series is a linear interpolation between them, so interpolated century-mean values differ slightly from raw point values; calBP convention is calBP = 1950 − CE (= 1950 + BCE), so the peak bin BCE 1400 ↔ calBP 3350. Openness/demographic proxies (pollen openness PC1 rising strongly after ~BCE 800; kde/growth rates) are context only and do not alter the capital-centric conclusion.

payload.hypothesis: Summed Social Capital (ZCU_AU Copper&Gold + Zamber Amber + ZMonument Monument Count) peaks in the century bin starting at BCE 1400 (14th century BCE, 1400-1301 BCE; CE -1400; calBP ~3350-3250) at 4.238, tied in raw 100-yr-sampled values at BCE 1300 but resolved unambiguously to BCE 1400 by the interpolated century-binned series. The only social-capital component that increases around/after this peak is Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU): 2.540 at the peak bin, rising to a short-window (BCE 1300-1200) mean of 2.695 and to its own maximum 2.850 at BCE 1200 (two centuries later than the summed peak), before the whole complex declines after ~BCE 1100 (long-window mean 0.901, slope -0.004/century). Amber (peak-bin -0.010 -> short mean -0.295, long mean -0.614, own max 1.540@BCE 3300) and Monument Count (peak-bin 1.708 -> short mean 1.530, long mean 0.147, own max 3.949@BCE 2700) do NOT increase after the peak and decline in both post-peak windows.
payload.workflow: 1) Parsed comma-decimal z-values in capital.csv (authoritative), oriented by ascending CE, summed SocialCapital = ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument per 100-yr bin. 2) Verified identity with time_series raw at 37 century points (max diff 0.0) and cross-checked peak with century-binned _inter interpolated sum. 3) Located summed-sum peak (BCE 1400, 4.238). 4) For each component computed value at total-peak bin, immediate ~200-yr post-peak window mean (BCE 1300-1200), full post-peak window (BCE 1300-500) mean, OLS slope per century over the full window, and own-peak century/value; classified increase by short-window rise above peak-bin value and/or own peak later than total peak. 5) Kept openness/demographic proxies (pollen PC1, kde/growth) strictly as context on the overlapping span.
